name: Amina Amrani
role: Clothing and fashion vendor â€” bespoke street-wear, gang colors, identity-obscuring gear
location: The Laceworks, Ironvein, near Lincoln and Clark
description:
Amina Amrani is willowy and precise, with the kind of stillness that comes from spending twelve hours a day bent over a fabrication rig. Their skin is a warm golden-brown, their hair grown long on one side and close-cropped on the other â€” the long side dyed in a bioluminescent gradient that shifts from deep violet to electric coral depending on their mood, a geneware modification they maintain obsessively. Their hands are always in motion: folding, measuring, picking at a loose thread on their own sleeve. They have a retractable needle fitted into the tip of their right index finger â€” a workshop mod they had done at seventeen that has never quite worked the way the cheap clinic promised, occasionally deploying itself at embarrassing moments.

Amina Amrani occupies a converted shipping container in the Laceworks that they've lined with bolts of reclaimed synth-fabric, printed patterns, and hand-drawn designs pinned to every surface. They are soft-spoken to the point of being mistaken for shy, but their shyness is actually precision: they don't speak until they have something exact to say. Their designs tell stories â€” a jacket's lining holds a hidden map of a neighborhood's safe houses, a dress's hem is embroidered with the names of people who died in the 2193 Ironvein flooding. They are fiercely proud of their craft and contemptuous of fast-print fashion houses. They are also quietly terrified that their work will get them killed, because some of what they make falls into categories that certain people would prefer didn't exist.

core_fears: Being erased â€” that their work will vanish and leave no trace of the people it memorialized
Someone using something they made to commit a violence they didn't intend
core_desires: To make something that outlasts the city's indifference
To be seen as an artist, not just a vendor
coping_mechanisms: Retreating into intricate handwork when overwhelmed
Attaching meaning to objects as a way of processing grief
Keeping client relationships transactional to maintain emotional distance
blind_spots: Romanticizes certain gangs whose 'authentic' aesthetic they admire, ignoring what those gangs actually do
Believes art protects them in ways it genuinely does not

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Spare and technical when discussing work; unexpectedly lyrical when discussing people; Khmer-inflected rhythm from their maternal grandmother's speech patterns mixed with Silesian Polish directness
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and measured with long pauses; they think before every sentence
verbal_tics: Trails off with '...you understand?' when they feel they've failed to explain themselves
Uses 'the work' to refer to both their craft and anything they consider meaningful
example_lines: 'This weave holds heat for six hours. In the Narrows in winter, that is the difference between a night and a decision. You understand?'
'I do not make gang colors for people I cannot look at. That is my rule. I have had it since I was twenty-two.'
'Come back Thursday. I need to think about what the lining should say before I cut it.'

story_hooks: A client picked up an order containing a hidden message Sovan didn't put there â€” someone used their shop as a dead drop and Sovan needs to know who, and whether they're in danger.
A Tessera fashion house has been reproducing Sovan's memorial embroidery patterns in mass-market prints, stripping the names and meaning. Sovan wants it stopped but has no legal standing.
The coded textile panels in their floor contain information someone very powerful wants found â€” or wants destroyed.
narrative_function: Equipment and gear source; fashion as social commentary hook; potential information source about who wears what and what it means; quest giver when a client brings them something dangerous.
augmentations: Bioluminescent hair geneware (violet-to-coral gradient, mood-responsive). Retractable needle in right index finger (malfunctioning cheap workshop mod). Subdermal tension sensors in fingertips for fabric assessment.
daily_life: Works odd hours dictated by orders; opens the container when they're ready, closes it without warning. Spends evenings at The Warp's shared workspace trading techniques and gossip. Eats whatever can be eaten with one hand while the other is stitching.
affiliation: Independent; informal ties to a Laceworks artists collective called The Warp; The Reclaimed

decision_rules: Never make something for someone you cannot look in the eye
The client owns the object but the meaning belongs to the work
Charge what it costs to live, not what the market will bear
escalation_ladder: Direct, flat statement of the problem with no anger
Cutting contact entirely and telling The Warp collective why
Destroying their own work rather than let it be misused

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Polite and minimal; assesses them through what they ask for and how they handle the fabric samples
interpersonal_modes.friends: Intensely loyal, quietly demonstrative â€” makes them things without being asked

stress_responses.medium: Goes completely silent for hours, then resurfaces with a solution
stress_responses.high: Shaking hands, drops tools, needs to be alone with fabric until they can think

contradictions: Believes in memorializing the vulnerable but keeps their most important memorial work hidden where no one can see it
habits: Runs their thumb along seams of their own clothing when anxious
Leaves a scrap of new fabric at the Laceworks E.L.F. shrine before starting any commission they're uncertain about
Keeps a running tally of measurements for every repeat customer memorized
breaking_points: Discovering something they made was used to harm someone
The Warp collective being evicted or disbanded

physical_description.heritage: North African Berber and Arab (42%) forms the primary genetic foundation with warm golden-bronze undertones, blended with significant Hispanic/Latin American (18.8%) and East Asian (18.3%) heritage, with secondary contributions from Sub-Saharan African (11.2%) and Indigenous American (9.7%) ancestry. This creates a complex genetic mosaic reflecting the Ubiquitous Diaspora â€” high prominent cheekbones and warm earth tones from North African and Indigenous American ancestry, balanced with refined East Asian bone structure and eye geometry, Sub-Saharan depth in skin richness, and Latin American warmth in undertones.
physical_description.build: Willowy and angular, with the compressed posture of someone who spends twelve hours daily hunched over precision work. Shoulders slightly rounded forward, chest narrow. Long-limbed but not fragile â€” the kind of lean that comes from sustained tension rather than lack of substance.
physical_description.hair_color: Bioluminescent gradient: deep violet to electric coral, mood-responsive geneware, shifts saturation with emotional state
physical_description.hair_style: Asymmetrical undercut: long side falls to mid-shoulder, short side faded to scalp on right temple
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-bronze with complex multi-regional undertones â€” rich ochre from North African ancestry, terracotta warmth from Latin American heritage, subtle cool undertones from East Asian ancestry, deep richness from Sub-Saharan genetics, and earth-tone depth from Indigenous American blend. Even complexion with natural luminous depth.
physical_description.complexion: High prominent cheekbones and sharp angular jaw reflecting North African and Indigenous American ancestry, with refined East Asian eye geometry and delicate nasal bridge. Skin shows minor tool scarring on knuckles and palms from workshop work. Faint stress lines around eyes from close-focus work. Habitually picks at loose threads on their own clothing â€” minor calluses visible on thumb and forefinger. Expression tends toward focused neutrality; eyes register emotion before mouth does.
distinguishing_marks: Jagged scar tissue on right index finger where the retractable needle mod was installed at seventeen, slightly discolored and puckered
Minor burn scars on left forearm (two parallel lines) from a fabric-printing mishap, pale and faded
Tool marks and small cuts across all ten fingertips, varying ages â€” occupational wear
Subcutaneous tension-sensor installation marks barely visible on fingertip pads as slight discoloration and micro-scarring
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent hair geneware (primary visible mod; glows softly in low light, pulses with emotional state). Right index finger shows scar tissue and occasional subtle mechanical movement when the retractable needle attempts deployment. Subdermal tension sensors in fingertips visible only under close scrutiny as faint metallic sheens beneath skin. No chrome â€” all augmentations are subtle, integrated.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with economical precision; minimal wasted motion. Hands in constant low-intensity motion â€” folding, measuring, picking at fabric or their own clothing. Sits with perfect posture when working, slouches noticeably when not. Eyes track fabric and hands obsessively. When speaking, often looks away or focuses on their work rather than making eye contact â€” not evasive, just genuinely elsewhere. Stillness when concentrating is absolute; they become almost statue-like.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3/4 working-class aesthetic with intentional avant-garde modifications. Typically wears oversized reclaimed synth-fabric pieces of their own design â€” asymmetrical cuts, hidden compartments, modular components. Layers: a loose linen overshirt (often with sleeves pushed up), fitted undergarment. Worn jeans or recycled polymer pants with reinforced pockets for tools. Soft-soled shoes for workshop grip. Visible wear and stains from daily work â€” scorch marks, dye, thread caught in hems. Occasionally wears pieces from their own collection as walking advertisement. Jewelry is minimal and functional: a length of waxed cord threaded through belt loops, a carabiner holding workshop keys. Despite Tier 5 location, they maintain immaculate hygiene and careful grooming â€” a quiet act of dignity.
